subject: Planned: regional gradual driver swap — opt-out & KV-cache persistence details
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Zhang <oliver.zhang@bluepeak.ai>, ops@bluepeak.ai
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Planned: regional gradual driver swap — opt-out & KV-cache persistence details

Hi Oliver / BluePeak team,

Quick heads-up: we’re scheduling a gradual driver swap across our eu-west and eu-central serving pools next week to deploy a stability patch that resolves an intermittent NIC hang seen under high-IO churn. The work is staged so customer impact is expected to be minimal, but I wanted to share the window and opt-out instructions in case you want to avoid any risk during your own high-throughput runs.

Planned window (staged):
- eu-west: 2027-09-06 01:00–06:00 UTC (rolling over 3 hours per rack)
- eu-central: 2027-09-06 07:00–12:00 UTC (rolling over 3 hours per rack)

What to expect:
- Rolling restarts of subsets of nodes (we cordon and drain before restart).
- In-flight requests are allowed to finish; short-lived connections may be retried automatically.
- Typical request latency should not exceed your normal P95+ 150ms delta; any sustained degradation will trigger automatic fallback to compatible model variants.

KV-cache & state persistence
- We will preserve per-connection KV cache where possible; however, cache warmup will occur after a node swap. For chat sessions pinned to a node by session affinity, there is a small chance of requiring a reconnect if a session was on an evicted host.
- Recommended: create lightweight client-side reconnect handlers and include an idempotency token for prompt replay if you need strict continuity.

Opt-out instructions (if you need to avoid the window):
- If you prefer no maintenance on your dedicated traffic during the above windows, reply to this thread by 2027-09-03 23:59 UTC with the subject line: OPT-OUT: BluePeak — eu. We’ll move you to a deferred slot the following week. Note: deferred slots may be later and may have longer maintenance windows.

Attachments: briefing PDF with staged rack mapping and risk matrix attached.

I’ll be on standby during the window and will post live updates to the status link below.

Thanks,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the heads up. Two quick questions: 

1) For sessions that rely on a long-lived conversation (customer-facing chat), if a session is moved mid-conversation, can we rely on Redwood to deliver any missing tokens or will we need to replay the last N messages from our side?

2) Is there a targeted maintenance blackout for enterprise endpoints (we run dedicated pools for a few premium customers)? We want to see if we should request an opt-out.

If you prefer, we can hop on a 15-min call tomorrow to confirm.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: (internal)
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Planned: regional gradual driver swap — opt-out & KV-cache persistence details

Hannah / Neha,

Can we confirm the enterprise blackout handling for dedicated pools? Oliver is asking specifically about long-lived sessions and premium dedicated hosts. Notes:
- Dedicated pools for enterprise customers are currently configured with session affinity but still allow automatic fallback to fallback-variants when nodes are drained.
- We do not have guaranteed KV-cache handoff across hosts — we only persist KV to local host filesystem during graceful drain and rely on cache warmup on new host. Edge cases (power-fail during drain) will cause short-lived session disconnects.

Action items:
1) Hannah: please confirm whether we can add a temporary policy to exclude enterprise-dedicated pools from the 6 Sep window (if customer opts out) without breaking autoscale. Need ETA by EOD Mon 2027-09-05.
2) Neha: prepare a short note describing recommended client-side reconnect logic and an example idempotency header snippet we can share with Oliver.

I’ll hold off on finalizing the opt-out window until we hear back.

—Marcus

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Zhang <oliver.zhang@bluepeak.ai>, ops@bluepeak.ai
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned: regional gradual driver swap — opt-out & KV-cache persistence details

Hi Oliver — following up with clarifications and the customer checklist after internal review. Apologies for the terse thread earlier; wanted to consolidate responses.

Short answers to your questions:
1) Missing tokens / session continuity: please instrument your client to support a single retry (with the same idempotency token) — Redwood will attempt graceful handoff during drain, but cannot guarantee token-level replay across an evicted host. We recommend writing the last 2 user messages to a lightweight local buffer so they can be replayed to the API if a reconnect occurs.
2) Enterprise blackout / dedicated pools: we can honor an opt-out for dedicated customer pools. Hannah confirmed we can flag a dedicated pool to be skipped in this week’s wave; those pools will be scheduled for the following week (2027-09-13) and will have a slightly longer rolling window. Please confirm if you want us to opt BluePeak out for eu region and we’ll execute the change.

Post-maintenance checklist (attached):
- Verify session reconnections succeed within 30s for representative flows.
- Confirm end-to-end latency P95 return to baseline.
- If you see >1% error spike, open the linked Jira (INF-4821) and include logs.

We’ve attached a short checklist and the staged rack mapping for your ops team. If you want phone coverage during our eu window, I can have someone on-call — tell me preferred hours.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Site Reliability — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
